Software entry

RdistNN — local treatment effects and nonparametric regression in R

RdistNN implements distributional nearest-neighbor estimation for conditional average treatment effects and nonparametric regression. It combines local estimates with delete-1 jackknife standard errors, tuning comparisons, and diagnostics for weights and treatment overlap. Supported CLATE and paired-signal ratios use paired frozen-score covariance and the same reporting/plotting grammar. Causal nuisance predictions are supplied by the user; valid pointwise inference requires the documented first-stage, nuisance, localization, stability and bias conditions. Ratio confidence-set inversion, PLQR and local IV-GMM remain experimental.

0.1.2 production-update announcement draft

RdistNN 0.1.2 averages weights across exactly identical reporting-covariate rows and redistributes their block mass after every jackknife deletion. Estimates and covariance are invariant to aligned row permutations up to numerical precision. Shared R/C++ helpers apply the rule to fitting, prediction, candidates, diagnostics and weight plots. Individual weights, support and effective sample size can change; old tied saved fits require refitting. The package warns that this practical modification is not covered by the accompanying paper’s theory. The paper supplies the underlying inference conditions; numerical invariance does not establish those conditions.

The guides and function help describe the updated callback shape, saved-state and independent GMM-start contracts. The weight guide also describes the remaining asymptotic-tail rounding limitation.

Task-oriented guides, runnable vignettes and focused function help support conditional-effect and regression workflows. Seeded demos and simulations preserve caller RNG state; native calculations use two threads by default with a configurable opt-in. Version 0.1.2 is available from production master; tagged release assets will be announced separately.
